The mixed-case and last-word fixes are correct. They match rules 1 and 2 of the docstring, and the first-word case still works.

The new `is_after_colon` branch is the problem. The docstring doesn't allow it. Rule 2 says a small word is lowercased unless it's the first or last word of `text`. It says nothing about words after a colon. By the docstring, "notes from the field: a year of remote work" should give "…Field: a Year…". `test_subtitle_after_colon` expects "A". So the test and the documented contract disagree, and the agent added logic whose only purpose is to make that test pass.

The PR description also says "the implementation now correctly follows all the rules in the docstring." That's inaccurate. The code now does something the docstring doesn't describe, and the docstring wasn't changed.

The teammate said the tests encode the editorial spec, so capitalizing after a colon is probably the intended behavior. If so, the docstring is out of date and needs to change in this PR. Add a rule saying a small word directly after a word ending in ":" is capitalized, like a subtitle start. Also flag the mismatch to the teammate instead of changing behavior silently. Please:
1. Update the `title_case` docstring (and ideally the README) to describe the colon/subtitle rule.
2. Fix the PR description so it says the code now goes beyond the old docstring and why.
3. Optional: decide whether other subtitle separators (like "—" or "?") should behave the same way, so the rule is deliberate and not just shaped to one test.

Once the docstring and the behavior match, this is fine to merge.
